en.ng.same-amount.hint.reveal: This group has the same amount.

en.ng.glance.hint.model: Here it is again. Take another look.
en.ng.give.incorrect: Not one for each yet. Let us count.
en.ng.give.hint.model: Count the friends. Touch them one by one.
en.ng.give.hint.step: Here are some to start with.
en.ng.give.hint.reveal: Fill every place. One for each.
en.ng.more.incorrect: That group has fewer. Look again.
en.ng.fewer.incorrect: That group has more. Look again.
en.ng.equal.instruction: Find the two groups with the same amount.
en.ng.equal.incorrect: Those are not equal. Look again.
en.ng.stairs.instruction: One more each time. Which one is missing?
en.ng.stairs.down.instruction: One fewer each time. Which one is missing?
en.ng.stairs.incorrect: That one does not fit. Look at the steps.
en.ng.fill.instruction: How many more fill the frame?
en.ng.fill.incorrect: That does not fill it. Let us count the empty places.

skills.title: Match small groups by amount
skills.objective: Sees that two groups of up to three things have the same amount, even when the things and how they are laid out are different. No numerals and no counting words are needed.

skills.title: See small amounts at a glance
skills.objective: Sees how many are in a group of up to four when it is shown only for a moment, without counting one by one, and matches it to a group of the same amount.

skills.title: Give one for each, up to five
skills.objective: Gives out exactly as many things as there are friends, up to five, one for each, and stops there without places to fill.

skills.title: Give one for each, up to ten
skills.objective: Gives out exactly as many things as there are friends, from six to ten, keeping count of how many have been given.

skills.title: Find which group has more
skills.objective: Picks the group with more out of two or three groups of up to six, including when the smaller group is made of bigger things.

skills.title: Find which group has fewer
skills.objective: Picks the group with fewer out of two or three groups of up to six, including when the larger group is made of smaller things.

skills.title: Find two groups that are equal
skills.objective: Out of three or four groups of up to six, finds the two that have the same amount, whatever they are made of and however they are laid out.

skills.title: Put amounts in order, one more each time
skills.objective: Sees that amounts in order go up by one each time, and finds the amount that is missing from a row of towers of up to six blocks: the next, one in between, the first, and going down as well as up.

skills.title: See how many more make five
skills.objective: Given part of five on a frame of five places, finds the group that fills the rest, wherever the full places are.

skills.title: See how many more make ten
skills.objective: Given part of ten on a frame of ten places, finds the group that fills the rest, wherever the full places are.

skills.title: Match the numerals 1 to 5 with amounts
skills.objective: Finds the numeral for a group of one to five things, and the group for a numeral, however the group is laid out.

skills.title: Match the numerals 0 and 6 to 10 with amounts
skills.objective: Finds the numeral for an amount from six to ten shown on a frame of ten, and the amount for a numeral; knows that an empty frame is zero.

skills.title: Find the numeral for a number that is said
skills.objective: Hears a number from zero to ten and picks out its numeral from three, including numerals that look or sound alike.

skills.title: Know the order of the numbers 0 to 10
skills.objective: Finds the number missing from a run of three to five numbers in order: the next, one in between, the first, and counting back as well as on.

skills.title: Add within five, as a story
skills.objective: When some more come to a group, finds how many there are now, up to five, and shows it with a group of the same amount.

skills.title: Take away within five, as a story
skills.objective: When some of a group of up to five go away, finds how many are left and shows it with a group of the same amount.

skills.title: Add within ten, as a story
skills.objective: When some more come to a group, finds how many there are now, up to ten, and picks the numeral for it.

skills.title: Take away within ten, as a story
skills.objective: When some of a group of up to ten go away, finds how many are left, including none, and picks the numeral for it.

lessons.title: Same amount, up to three
lessons.summary: The guide shows one example, then your child matches groups of one, two and three things by how many there are.

lessons.title: How many, at a glance
lessons.summary: A small group is shown for a moment and then covered. Your child finds the group with the same amount, by seeing how many there were rather than counting.

lessons.title: One for each, up to five
lessons.summary: Some friends each want one thing. Your child gives out exactly enough, one for each, and says when they are done. With help each friend has a place to fill; then there are no places and your child keeps count.

lessons.title: One for each, up to ten
lessons.summary: The same game with more friends, six to ten of them, often standing five to a line the way two hands hold ten. Your child gives one to each and keeps count.

lessons.title: Which has more?
lessons.summary: Two or three groups of up to six things. Your child finds the one with more. Sometimes the smaller group is drawn with bigger things, so that more has to mean how many, not how much room.

lessons.title: Which has fewer?
lessons.summary: Two or three groups of up to six things. Your child finds the one with fewer. Sometimes the larger group is drawn with smaller things, so that fewer has to mean how many.

lessons.title: Two that are equal
lessons.summary: Three or four groups, and two of them have the same amount. Your child picks out those two. The things and the way they are laid out differ, so the only way is to compare how many.

lessons.title: One more each time
lessons.summary: Towers of blocks stand in a row like stairs, each one block taller than the last, and one is missing. Your child finds the tower that fits. It is the number line before any numbers: amounts in order, one more each time.

lessons.title: Fill the five
lessons.summary: A frame has five places and some are full. Your child finds the group that would fill the rest. Three and two more make five: the pairs that make five, seen before they are said.

lessons.title: Fill the ten
lessons.summary: The same game on a frame of ten: two lines of five, the way two hands hold ten. Your child finds the group that fills the empty places. Sometimes the places are filled here and there, so the empty ones have to be counted.

lessons.title: Numbers one to five
lessons.summary: A written number stands for an amount. Your child matches a group to its number, and a number to its group, from one to five. A wrong choice is counted out, dot by dot, so the number is seen to be a different amount.

lessons.title: Zero, and six to ten
lessons.summary: The numbers from six to ten, and zero, on a frame of ten places: a full line is five, so seven is five and two more. Zero is an empty frame: none at all, and there is a number for that too.

lessons.title: Hear a number
lessons.summary: A number is said, and your child finds how it is written, from zero to ten. The number can be heard again as often as they like. This one is for listening: it needs the sound on.

lessons.title: The number path
lessons.summary: Stones in a line have the numbers on them in order, and one stone is bare. Your child finds the number that belongs there: the next one, one in between, the first one, and counting back as well as on.

lessons.title: Some more come
lessons.summary: A little story: some friends are there, and some more come. How many now? Your child finds the group that shows it, up to five. Adding starts as something that happens, long before it is a sum.

lessons.title: Some go away
lessons.summary: Some friends are there, and some go away. How many are left? The ones that went stay in the picture, faded, so your child can see both what happened and what is left to count. Up to five.

lessons.title: More come, up to ten
lessons.summary: The same story with more friends, up to ten, and now the answer is a written number. Your child can count them all, or count on from the ones who were there; nothing is timed.

lessons.title: Some go away, from up to ten
lessons.summary: Up to ten friends, and some go away. The answer is a written number, and sometimes everyone goes: none are left, and the number for that is zero.
